gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold issue concerns an undefined or malformed global dG-star interpolation estimate caused by applying a seminorm over the whole mesh to an interpolant defined only on K, and requires a corrected global interpolation bound. ISSUE-001 instead concerns the omitted accuracy condition on the discrete initial concentration and the initial energy term; it does not identify the interpolation-formula defect or its global-extension problem.

The gold issue concerns insufficient time regularity of acoustic and concentration source terms for the claimed classical well-posedness and Picard–Lindelöf argument. ISSUE-001 diagnoses only missing spatial accuracy of the discrete initial concentration and does not recognize the source-regularity hypothesis or the resulting C2/C1 existence failure.

Both identify the missing approximation requirement on the discrete initial concentration, the resulting initial error term that is dropped when integrating the energy estimate, and failure of the claimed O(h^{2q}) concentration bound for arbitrary u_0^h. The prediction also supplies the appropriate interpolation-based repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The concentration convergence estimate requires the initial discrete concentration error, equivalently ||I_h u_0-u_0^h|| or ||u_0-u_0^h||, to be O(h^q); without that condition the initial energy can be O(1) and the claimed rate does not follow.

component_coverage.gold_component: Missing initial approximation condition for the discrete concentration and the resulting uncontrolled initial energy term in the concentration error estimate.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-001 explicitly states that no condition is imposed on u_0^h, identifies the dropped initial discrete error in the integrated energy inequality, explains that arbitrary data can contradict the O(h^{2q}) rate, and gives u_0^h=I_hu_0 or an O(h^q) approximation as repair.
